author: Rory Robinson
title: Sue Bird slammed for visible reaction to comments clearly aimed at Caitlin Clark - NewsBreak
text:
By Rory Robinson ,
58 minutes ago Sue Bird is facing harsh criticism from WNBA fans, especially die-hard supporters of Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark, after a moment on her podcast that many interpreted as a mini shot at Clark and the wave of new fans following her rise.
The backlash stemmed from an episode featuring Katie Nolan released last Thursday where the sports podcaster described last season's tension within the league without naming a WNBA player. For many listeners, the identity felt obvious after previous pressures prompted Clark to address allegations of racism within her fan base.
The Casuals podcast host spoke about what she framed as growing pains for the WNBA, suggesting that some newer fans arrived for "a weird reason" and latched onto one specific player who, in their minds, stood at odds with what a WNBA player is supposed to be. Fans immediately attached the monologue to describing Clark .
• Team USA makes its feelings clear on Angel Reese comments about teammates
• Kim Mulkey shows her true colors with ruthless response to unbeaten LSU
As Nolan spoke, Bird appeared to smirk and nod along. Her visible reaction quickly circulated online and fans of the Fever star weren't happy about what they witnessed. Nolan still acknowledged that the unnamed player was "very, very good."
While Clark's name was never mentioned, fans believed the comments couldn't be directed elsewhere. Bird previously had to address claims of being "petty and jealous" of Clark during an earlier rendition of their show, despite publicly praising her game on national television .
Some listeners accused Bird of gatekeeping, while others said the exchange reinforced the very divide it claimed to critique.
"I'm done with this damn podcast. I do not trust Sue Bird," one user wrote. Another added, "My love is actually hate?!? I’m so sick of this faux psychology and gaslighting bull----."
Others cited their long-time NBA fan experiences, noting they didn't face similar hostility with stars like Michael Jordan, and questioned why women's basketball struggles to welcome growth for new fans.
Several fans pushed back against the characterization of Clark's fan base itself. One user argued that Clark's supporters are no different from any other star's following, except that it is "larger and more diverse", noting her international reach.
Another labeled Bird's response as "a wild mischaracterization of the problem," suggesting the issue lies less with fans and more with how the discussion is framed by influential voices in the sport like Bird.
Bird even recently praised Clark's approach to last year's injury-ridden season , during which she played in only 13 games after not missing a single one during her rookie season.
“The first thing that came to mind, and this comes to the whole Indiana Fever, they did a great job engaging in their season," said Bird. "I thought what was most impressive was the way she stayed engaged…that speaks to her maturity."
